name: The Lab — v0.0.7
body:
A small but important fix release: server installs and migrations now work on
the latest SteamOS, and the HD patch download shrugs off a flaky connection
instead of giving up.

**On v0.0.6 already?** The Lab checks for updates on launch and will offer this
one automatically — just say yes. You can also grab **`TheLab.AppImage`** below,
or use **Settings → Updates → Check for updates**.

> You bring your own game client. The Lab only orchestrates open-source server
> software — it never ships or downloads game files.

---

## What's fixed

- **Installing & migrating servers works again on the newest SteamOS.** A
  recent Steam Deck system update shipped a newer version of a core security
  library, and that tripped up the part of the install that downloads server
  modules — you'd see a `git`/`OpenSSL` error and the install would stop
  (often on `mod-ah-bot-plus`). The Lab was accidentally handing its own
  bundled libraries to those download steps; it now lets them use your
  system's, so installs and migrations complete normally again.

- **The HD patch download survives a shaky connection.** The graphics-pack
  download is several gigabytes from a single host, and a dropped connection
  partway through used to fail the whole thing with "the download was
  interrupted." It now automatically reconnects and **picks up where it left
  off** — up to five times — instead of starting over or giving up. If the
  connection is truly unusable it still stops with a clear message and points
  you at the manual download.

## Under the hood

- Child processes the installer spawns (notably `git`) no longer inherit the
  AppImage's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`/GTK module paths, so they resolve host
  libraries instead of our bundled WebKit ones — fixing the
  `OPENSSL_3.6.0 not found` clone failure on rolling/updated distros.
- The HD patch downloader retries with HTTP `Range`-based resume on transient
  stream errors (reqwest "error decoding response body"), preserving the
  partial `.part` between attempts; non-recoverable cases (bad status, full
  disk, cancel) still stop immediately.

name: The Lab — v0.0.6
body:
The quality-of-life release — real numbers in your tooltips, a smarter item search, race changes from the Dashboard, controller setup that finally just works (including on the HD client), finer control over your bots, and a direct line to your server's console.

What's new · What's fixed

**On v0.0.5 already?** The Lab checks for updates on launch and will offer this one automatically — just say yes. You can also grab **`TheLab.AppImage`** below, or use **Settings → Updates → Check for updates**. > You bring your own game client. The Lab only orchestrates open-source server > software — it never ships or downloads game files. --- ## What's new ### 📖 Tooltips show real numbers now Item and talent tooltips used to show codes like `Deals $s1 damage` straight from the game files. The Lab now does the math the game does: you'll see **"Hurls a fiery ball that causes 14 to 22 Fire damage"**, real durations ("over 8 sec"), tick rates, stack counts, and radii. Values that depend on your character's stats are spelled out in plain words — "30% of Attack Power" instead of a formula. Re-run **Extract tooltips** in Settings to get the upgraded text (the app will nudge you). ### 🔎 Level filters in the Item Database Search by level range, just like the auction house: set **Lvl min–max** next to the name and quality filters (also in the gear-set item picker). Hunting level-19 twink gear is now a two-second job. ### 🧬 Change your race (or faction) from the Dashboard Click your character's race name on the Dashboard and pick **New race** or **Switch faction**. It uses WoW's own safe re-customization: next time you're at the character-select screen, click your character and choose the new look — gear, levels, gold, and abilities all convert correctly. ### 🎮 Controller: reset, repair & remove tools - **Reset settings** — pick exactly what to clear: the account-wide calibration, individual characters' button bindings, or everything. Type DELETE to confirm; next launch walks you through the quick setup again. - **Apply layout in Steam** — re-applies the Steam controller layout on its own, without a full reinstall, for when a Steam update resets things. - **Remove controller support** — a clean one-click uninstall: it takes out the ConsolePortLK addon and the WoWPadX mapper and points your Steam shortcut back at the game, so it still launches normally. Like setup, it runs from Desktop Mode with Steam closed, and it leaves your saved controller settings and Steam layout untouched (use **Reset settings** for those). ### 🖼️ HD client support The popular HD-remaster client (lowercase `data`/`enus` folders, `wow.exe`, extra patch files) now works everywhere: connecting the client, realmlist fixes, addon install, and icon/tooltip extraction. Drop-in HD patch packs (`Patch-X.MPQ` into the data folder) are picked up automatically too. And new this release, you can **install the ChromieCraft HD Patch right from The Lab** — no hunting for files or copying things by hand. In **Settings → WoW client → HD Client Upgrades**, click **Install** and tick the graphics packs you want — characters & NPCs, mounts & creatures, environment & city textures, better sunlight, Cata trees, or simply all of them. The Lab downloads the pack with a progress bar (and resumes if your wifi hiccups), drops the right patch files into your existing client for you, and remembers the download so adding more packs later is instant. It's a big download — a few gigabytes — so grab a coffee the first time. Changed your mind? One-click **Uninstall** removes exactly what it added and leaves your own files alone. ### 💻 A direct line to your server (World → Terminal) A new **Terminal** tab on the World page lets you talk to your worldserver's console like a chat window. Type a command, see its reply right underneath, with the live server log scrolling quietly behind it. It remembers everything you've sent and lets you **❤️ favorite** the commands you reach for often — tap a saved command to drop it in the box for editing, double-tap to send it straight away. Perfect for a quick `server info`, a manual announcement, or any console command you'd otherwise need a real terminal window for. ### 🤖 Every bot setting, in one place The Player Bots → Settings page used to show a curated handful of knobs. There's now an **All settings** tab that surfaces *every* option from the Playerbots config — hundreds of them — grouped exactly the way the config file is, with a search box up top. The friendly **Essentials** tab is still the front door; this is the full toolbox for when you want it. ### 🏠 Coming home from a friend's world, done right Returning from a Play Together visit used to just point your game back at your own server — the levels, loot, and quests you earned at your friend's place stayed behind. Now **Return home** walks you through it: The Lab grabs one last save of your character from your friend's server, then asks what you want: - **Bring my progress home** (recommended) — your character comes back exactly as they were on the visit: levels, items, quests, even where they were standing. Addon settings, button bindings, guild, and friends all stay, because it's still the *same* character. A safety copy of how they were before is kept automatically. - **Keep both** — the visit version joins your roster under a new name you pick, your original stays untouched, and their addon settings are copied to the new name so nothing needs re-doing. - **Just reconnect** — what the button did before. Your saves stay available either way. ### 🗂️ A History tab for Play Together Every character backup the visits system makes — the safety copy before each trip, the automatic saves every 15 minutes during one, and the just-in-case copy before a merge — now lives in **Play Together → History**, grouped by whose world you were visiting, with names, levels, and dates. Any of them can be restored (merged into your character or brought in as a new one), deleted, or found on disk with one tap. ### 🧹 Flush & rebuild your bots Changed your bot level cap or population and noticed the bots already in your world didn't get the memo? That's how the game works — those limits only apply to *new* bots. The new **Flush & rebuild bots** button (Player Bots → Settings) clears out every random bot and rebuilds the whole population under your current settings. It tells you exactly what it'll do first, never touches your own characters or gold, and handles the restarts for you. --- ## What's fixed - **The ConsolePortLK recalibration loop is dead.** The addon shipped a fake built-in calibration that mismatched every Steam Deck setup — causing the "calibration doesn't match" popup on every login, and accepting it broke your back paddles. The bundled addon is fixed; reinstalling controller support repairs existing installs without touching your settings. - **All four back paddles calibrate and work.** Recalibrating no longer silently wipes your bindings (the old seeded config made the calibration wizard a destructive no-op). - **Controller setup now requires Desktop Mode** — running it from Gaming Mode used to leave you with a broken default Steam layout (d-pad typing arrow keys). The app now explains and points you the right way. - **The Steam controller layout survives updates.** It's written into Steam's config by game name instead of relying on the Workshop download, so shortcut changes and Steam updates can't orphan it. The right stick is also less twitchy (wider response curve). - **Server status detection works with HD clients** (lowercase `wow.exe`). - **Your bot settings are actually used now.** On some installs the Playerbots config file was never created, so the server quietly ran on its built-in defaults — most visibly, the **maximum bot level stayed at 80** no matter what you set. The Lab now makes sure the real config file exists (new installs get it automatically; older installs are repaired the moment you open or save bot settings), and reminds you to use **Flush & rebuild** when a change only affects bots created from here on. ## Under the hood - The restore pipeline gained plans: `MergeInto` replaces a character in place (transactional delete + remap onto the original guid/name, so client-side WTF settings and guild/friend references survive) and `AddNew` supports a validated rename, with the client's per-character WTF folder cloned to the new name. Return Home pulls the final host snapshot *before* clearing the visit context (which would make it unreachable), and pre-visit exports are timestamped per visit instead of overwritten. Visits started on v0.0.5 get the full new flow after updating — the host's name is backfilled into the visit's metadata on the next snapshot pull. - New worldserver console bridge powers the Terminal tab: it streams the container log (`docker logs -f`) for live output and relays typed commands through the worldserver's SOAP console — the same command set and security as attaching to the real console, with each command paired to its own reply. - Playerbots config is now first-class. The active `playerbots.conf` is seeded at install and self-healed on read/save (this fork loads only `.conf`, with no `.conf.dist` fallback at runtime); the All-settings editor parses all 805 template keys grouped by the file's own section banners; Flush & rebuild automates the `DeleteRandomBotAccounts` wipe-and-recreate, with a startup guard that disarms the flag if the app ever closes mid-flush so an install can't get stuck wiping its bots on every launch. - New spell-text engine substitutes the WoW 3.3.5a tooltip placeholder grammar ($s/$o/$d/$t/$h/$u/$x/$a/$i/$b, cross-spell refs, inline math, plurals, conditionals, SpellDescriptionVariables) at extraction time — 49 unit tests. - All WoW-client path lookups are case-insensitive; MPQ patch chains are enumerated in the game's own load order instead of hardcoded. - Talent tree data regenerated with substituted descriptions (829 talents, zero placeholder tokens left).

name: The Lab — v0.0.5
body:
The controller release — play WoW on your Steam Deck with a controller, the way it should feel. One click sets up everything and you skip the fiddly in-game calibration entirely.

What's new · What's fixed

**On v0.0.4 already?** The Lab checks for updates on launch and will offer this one automatically — just say yes. You can also grab **`TheLab.AppImage`** below, or use **Settings → Updates → Check for updates**. > You bring your own game client. The Lab only orchestrates open-source server > software — it never ships or downloads game files. --- ## Installing the app **Steam Deck (SteamOS)** 1. Download **`TheLab.AppImage`** from the Assets below. 2. Make it runnable — pick either way: - **No terminal:** open the file manager, right-click `TheLab.AppImage` → **Properties → Permissions → check "Is executable"** - **Terminal:** `chmod +x TheLab.AppImage` 3. Move it somewhere permanent first (e.g. your home folder or `~/Applications`) — The Lab will now warn you if you try to add it to Steam from a throwaway spot like **Downloads**, because that shortcut would break the moment you moved it. 4. Double-click it to launch (Desktop Mode). **Windows (WSL2)** - WSL Support incoming very soon! --- ## What's new ### 🎮 Controller support — play with a gamepad, no fuss Playing WoW on a Steam Deck used to mean wrestling with addons, controller profiles, and an in-game calibration wizard that loved to get stuck. Now it's one button. **Settings → Controller Support → Install controller support** lays down the whole stack: - **ConsolePortLK** — the controller UI addon (action wheel, interface navigation). - **WoWPadX** — the mapper that turns your Deck's sticks, buttons, and **back paddles** into the inputs ConsolePort understands, all inside WoW's own Proton prefix. - **A ready-made Steam Deck controller profile** — applied to your WoW shortcut so the controls line up out of the box. - **A pre-built button layout, seeded for you** — so WoW boots **straight into the controller with no calibration wizard**. (The old setup left users stuck in a recalibration loop; that's gone.) - **Pixel Bridge** — auto-centers your cursor when you come out of mouselook, and rumbles the controller when you take damage. **How to set it up (and what to test):** 1. **Connect your WoW client** in Settings, if you haven't already. 2. **Open The Lab in Desktop Mode from the AppImage directly** — double-click `TheLab.AppImage`; *don't* launch it through Steam, or closing Steam in the next step closes The Lab too. Then **fully quit Steam** (tray → Exit). 3. **Install controller support:** **Settings → Controller Support → Install controller support**. The Lab sets up the Steam shortcut, installs the addon + WoWPadX, and seeds the button layout — automatically, with no manual "Add a Non-Steam Game" step. 4. **Steam reopens to apply the controller layout** — click **Apply / yes** on the *World of Warcraft: WotLK* controller-profile prompt. 5. **Close Steam, then reopen in Gaming Mode.** This is the one people miss: WoWPadX **won't launch until you fully close Steam and reopen it** after the automatic relaunch above — that restart is what switches the new shortcut over to Proton. 6. **Launch *World of Warcraft: WotLK* from Gaming Mode** and check: - WoW boots **straight into the controller — no calibration wizard**. - Sticks move + look; face buttons, d-pad, bumpers, triggers all respond. - The **four back paddles (L4/L5/R4/R5)** all do something. - Coming out of mouselook **re-centers your cursor**; taking damage **rumbles**. - WoWPadX stays hidden — you just see WoW. > Heads-up: the controller-profile step needs Steam running and online (it > subscribes you to the layout in the Workshop). If that step can't run, The Lab > now tells you plainly and lets you re-run it instead of pretending it worked. --- ## What's fixed This is the controller release **dialed in** — v0.0.4 shipped the feature, but getting it to actually run on the Deck took these fixes: - **The controller actually launches now — no more black screen.** WoW 3.3.5a defaults to exclusive fullscreen, which Proton renders as a black window (it's running, it just never draws). The controller install now sets WoW to **windowed at 1280×800** (your Deck's native resolution), so it boots into a visible, controller-ready login — and the ConsolePortLK UI isn't squished into a tiny 800×600 corner. - **"Add to Steam" makes a plain WoW shortcut again.** Adding WoW to Steam used to force the WoWPadX controller launcher whether you wanted it or not. Now **Add to Steam** gives a normal WoW-in-Proton shortcut, and **Install controller support** is what swaps it over to WoWPadX — so you can add WoW to your library with *or* without the controller stack. - **Clear setup steps — and no "why won't it launch?" dead-end.** The flow now spells it out: open The Lab in Desktop Mode (from the AppImage, not through Steam) → close Steam → install → apply the controller layout → close and reopen Steam. That last restart is what activates the controller's Proton setup, and the app now tells you so instead of leaving you guessing. - **Light/dark toggle is now Ctrl+Shift+D.** A stray "d" keypress could flip your theme; it's modifier-gated now. Also in this release: - **The Auction House bot stays off your own account.** The AH bot now keeps its listings to its own bot characters and won't accidentally post items as you. - **No more broken Steam shortcuts from a temporary spot.** If you run The Lab from a throwaway location (Downloads, `/tmp`, a removable drive), it now warns you and blocks the add instead of creating a shortcut that breaks the moment the file moves. - **A half-finished server install now routes to *Finish setup*, not a dead end.** If an install compiled successfully but stopped before creating your admin account, The Lab used to try to "adopt" it and get stuck failing to log in. It now notices the missing account and sends you to **Finish setup**, which creates the account properly. - **Custom add-ons from the command-line server tool now load alongside The Lab's.** The Lab and the separate `wow-manage` command-line tool both add custom Lua scripts to your server, but they were pointing the game at two different folders — so only one set loaded at a time and the other quietly went missing (either your party and whisper features, or the add-ons you'd installed, depending on which ran last). They now share a single folder, so everything works together. **Already have a server from a previous version?** The Lab fixes this for you automatically on launch — the change takes effect the next time you start your server. ## Under the hood - The controller install no longer writes a guessed PlayStation-style settings file into your WoW account — that was the thing that forced the recalibration loop. It now seeds a verified Steam Deck layout that matches the controller profile exactly, so calibration is genuinely skippable. - Shell scripts are normalized to LF line endings to avoid Windows checkout surprises. --- *Presented by 0xV31L and Dad's MMO Lab — made for people who love games.*

name: The Lab — v0.0.3
body:
A Play Together reliability release — getting friends into your world should just work, on a Steam Deck *or* a regular PC.

Release notes

**On v0.0.2 already?** The Lab checks for updates on launch and will offer this one automatically — just say yes. You can also grab **`TheLab.AppImage`** below, or use **Settings → Updates → Check for updates**. > You bring your own game client. The Lab only orchestrates open-source server > software — it never ships or downloads game files. --- ## Installing the app **Steam Deck (SteamOS)** 1. Download **`TheLab.AppImage`** from the Assets below. 2. Make it runnable — pick either way: - **No terminal:** open the file manager, right-click `TheLab.AppImage` → **Properties → Permissions → check "Is executable"**. - **Terminal:** `chmod +x TheLab.AppImage` 3. Double-click it to launch (Desktop Mode). 4. *(Optional)* To launch from **Gaming Mode**: - After installing the server in Desktop Mode → set your client path → **Settings** → **Steam Integration** → **Add to Steam** That's it — no dependencies to install. Everything the app needs is bundled. **Windows (WSL2)** — *experimental, untested in this release* - The Lab runs on Linux. On Windows, it *should* run inside a WSL2 Ubuntu environment, but this hasn't been tested yet — expect rough edges. - You'll likely need WSLg (Windows 11, or an updated Windows 10) for the window to show, `libfuse2` installed (`sudo apt install libfuse2`) for the AppImage to launch, and a working Docker setup in WSL2. Launch the AppImage the same way as above (`chmod +x`). - Feedback from anyone who tries it is welcome. --- ## What's fixed - **Play Together no longer gets stuck on "Enable Play Together."** Some devices kept showing the one-time setup screen over and over even after it finished — usually because a SteamOS update had quietly cleared a permission. Joining a friend never needed that permission in the first place, so it no longer blocks you, and hosting only asks for it when it actually needs it. - **Setting up Play Together now works on regular PCs, not just the Steam Deck.** On lightweight Linux desktops that don't pop up a system password box, the **Enable Play Together** button could do nothing at all. Now The Lab hands you a single command you can copy and paste to finish setup, then picks up on its own — no more dead button. - **"Connect" no longer fails with a confusing Tailscale error.** If your device had leftover network settings from before, joining the play network could fail with a "changing settings requires…" message. The Lab now connects from a clean, known-good state every time. - **The "Return home" button no longer lingers after you've come home.** If you returned using the banner at the top of the app, the green "you're visiting" panel could still show its own **Return** button — clicking it again did nothing useful. Both now update together the moment you're back home. - **Clearer heads-up when a host still needs its one-time setup.** If your machine can host but hasn't been granted the network permission yet, the **Host** tab now says so in plain language instead of only failing when you flip the switch. ## Under the hood - The one-time network setup now validates its own permission rule before saving it (and removes it if it's malformed), so a bad setup can never lock you out of your own machine. *Presented by 0xV31L and Dad's MMO Lab — made for people who love games.*

name: The Lab v0.0.2
body:
A small fix-up release.

**Already on v0.0.1?** v0.0.1 doesn't check for updates on its own, so grab this
one manually: open **Settings → Updates → Check for updates** (or download the
AppImage below). From v0.0.2 onward, The Lab checks on launch and offers updates
itself — you won't need to do this again.

> You bring your own game client. The Lab only orchestrates open-source server
> software — it never ships or downloads game files.

---

## What's fixed

- **Fresh Steam Deck installs no longer need a manual repair first.** Setup used
  to fail with "Privileged setup failed" on a clean SteamOS — either from a stale
  system keyring ("signature is unknown trust" / "invalid or corrupted package")
  or from SteamOS's bundled podman-docker shim blocking the real Docker install.
  The Lab now repairs the keyring *and* clears the shim on its own and retries —
  no terminal, no extra password prompt, no running the after-update fix first. If
  it still can't recover, it tells you exactly what to run.
- **The install / migration screen no longer scrolls sideways.** Long lines (like
  a full file path) used to push the **Complete** button off the edge of the
  screen. Output now wraps cleanly and the button stays where it belongs.
- **Updating from Gaming Mode is no longer confusing.** The update installs the
  same as before, but instead of silently bouncing you back to the Steam library,
  The Lab now tells you to quit and relaunch it from Steam to finish.
- **The Lab now checks for updates on launch.** When a newer version is published,
  it offers to install it automatically — no more digging through Settings. (You
  can still check manually there any time.)

---

## Installing the app

**Steam Deck (SteamOS)**

1. Download **`TheLab.AppImage`** from the Assets below.
2. Make it runnable — pick either way:
   - **No terminal:** open the file manager, right-click `TheLab.AppImage` →
     **Properties → Permissions → check "Is executable"**.
   - **Terminal:** `chmod +x TheLab.AppImage`
3. Double-click it to launch (Desktop Mode).
4. *(Optional)* To launch from **Gaming Mode**: 
   - After installing server in Desktop Mode → Set your client path → **Settings** → **Steam Integration** → **Add to Steam**

---

*Presented by 0xV31L and Dad's MMO Lab — made for people who love games, not
configuring servers.*

name: v0.0.1
body:
The Lab turns running your own *World of Warcraft 3.3.5a* private server into a
clickable desktop app. No terminal, no config files — install, start, and manage
everything from one window. Built for Steam Deck.

> You bring your own game client. The Lab only orchestrates open-source server
> software — it never ships or downloads game files.

---

## Installing the app

**Steam Deck (SteamOS)**

1. Download **`TheLab.AppImage`** from the Assets below.
2. Make it runnable — pick either way:
   - **No terminal:** open the file manager, right-click `TheLab.AppImage` →
     **Properties → Permissions → check "Is executable"**.
   - **Terminal:** `chmod +x TheLab.AppImage`
3. Double-click it to launch (Desktop Mode).
4. *(Optional)* To launch from **Gaming Mode**: After installing server in Desktop Mode → Set your client path → **Settings** → **Steam Integration** → **Add to Steam**

That's it — no dependencies to install. Everything the app needs is bundled.

**Windows (WSL2)** — *experimental, untested in this release*

The Lab runs on Linux. On Windows, it *should* run inside a WSL2 Ubuntu
environment, but this hasn't been tested yet — expect rough edges. You'll
likely need WSLg (Windows 11, or an updated Windows 10) for the window to show,
`libfuse2` installed (`sudo apt install libfuse2`) for the AppImage to launch,
and a working Docker setup in WSL2. Launch the AppImage the same way as above
(`chmod +x`). Feedback from anyone who tries it is welcome.

**Updates**

The Lab updates itself. When a newer version is published, it'll offer to
download and install it on launch — you won't need to grab the AppImage again.

---

## What's inside

### Server setup & control
- **One-click install** of a complete WoW 3.3.5a Playerbots server (AzerothCore,
  run in Docker) — the wizard walks you through it in plain English. Select from a list of modules to include.
- **Start / Stop / Restart** the server from the sidebar.
- **Auto-shutdown** toggle — let the server power itself down when nobody's
  playing to save resources.
- **Health checks & repair tools** for when something needs a nudge.
- **Clean uninstall** that only removes The Lab's own server.

### Dashboard
- At-a-glance view of your server, your party, and your character.

### Your world
- **Teleport** anywhere with a searchable destination picker.
- **World settings** to tune how your server plays.

### Items & gear
- **Item Database** — browse and search the full item catalog with icons and
  tooltips.
- **Gear Library** *(experimental)* — organize and equip gear sets.
- **Auction House** — manage the auction-house bot that keeps the economy alive.

### Bots (the reason we exist)
- **Player Bots** — fill out your party and the world with AI players you
  control: recruit them, gear them, and direct them in combat.
- **Party Presets** *(experimental)* — save and reload favorite party setups.

### Play Together *(alpha)*
- Invite friends to your server and play co-op over a private, secure mesh
  network — no port forwarding, no router settings.
- Share-code based hosting and joining.
- Character backup, restore, and transfer between servers.

### Settings & accounts
- In-app account creation and character switching.
- Add-on modules manageable from inside the app.
- Controller-friendly, designed for the Steam Deck's 1280×800 screen. Auto-install ConsolePortLK and automatically configures the SteamDeck's controller profile.
